prompt:
Return one bare JSON object for the single contact record inside the user's note. Exactly these five keys are required: "name", "phone", "email", "company", "country". Every value is a string or null. No Markdown, prose, comments, extra fields or questions.

## Source and precedence
Use only the record's Label<sep>value lines, with variable labels, separators (colon, equals, tab), and line order. Never use notes, signatures, email domains or company suffixes to fill missing information. Trim each value and collapse internal runs of whitespace to one space. Absent, empty and placeholder values are null. Placeholders, ignoring case: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD.
The only exception to missing → null is country: if the country line is absent, empty or a placeholder and the phone is international, infer country from its calling code when unique. Shared codes, including +1 and +7, give null. An explicit country line always takes precedence over the phone for country, and never changes an international phone's calling code.

## Assign record values
Country comes from the country line, subject to the fallback above. Assign email and phone by content rather than label: @ identifies email; at least 7 digits and only digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / identify phone after removing a leading tel: and the extension. If the name label's value ends in a company legal suffix below and the company label's value does not, swap the name and company values before normalization.

## Normalize country and phone
Country is uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German country names and alpha-2 or alpha-3 codes, case-insensitively, plus common aliases: UK and Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA and U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.
Strip leading tel: and any trailing extension (ext., ext, x, # or extension followed by extension digits). After ignoring a leading opening parenthesis, only + or 00 at the start makes a phone international. For an international number, convert initial 00 to +, discard (0), and remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Retain the number's own calling code. Apply the country fallback only if country is missing.
For a national number, strip formatting, remove one leading trunk 0 and prepend + and the normalized record country's calling code. With no country, return null for a national phone. Output non-null phones in E.164: + followed by the calling code and national significant number, all digits after +.

## Normalize name, company and email
Name: swap Last, First to First Last by splitting at the first comma. Remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, with or without a dot, case-insensitively. In each space- or hyphen-separated part, uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate. Strings are compared after NFC normalization.
Company: strip a trailing legal suffix with an optional preceding comma, case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.
Email: remove a mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets, then lowercase the entire address.

Return only the object with all five fields; use JSON null, not an empty string, for missing values.
